It is contended by the counsel for the appellant that in the present case pertaining to an incident Abhishek Kushwaha vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 16 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/70169039/

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The counsel contends that the entire case of the prosecution is baseless and there is false implication of the present petitioner.
The counsel contends that the appellant as well as respondents were in relationship and even they applied for registration of marriage.

It is further contended by the counsel that the appellant has not committed any offence and he was not confronted with any criminal case in past and if the appellant is taken into custody in connection with the offence in question the same would cause immense hardship as well as prejudice to the petitioner thus taking into consideration this fact as also the fact that the appellant as well as complainant are willing to enter into wedlock the present application deserves to be allowed.
3.
Per contra counsel for the State submits that the present application filed by the petitioner deserves to be dismissed.
It is contended by the counsel that there is false promise at the behest of the appellant to enter into marriage.

It is contended by the counsel that the statement of prosecutrix recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C reveals that rape was committed with the prosecutrix under the garb of false promise of marriage and the prosecutrix has repeated her version in the statement recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C on 29.1.2024 that despite there being assurance by the appellant,
the appellant is not ready to perform marriage with the prosecutrix.
Thus, the present appeal deserves to be dismissed.

4. Having considered the submissions advanced on behalf of the parties, it is relevant from perusal of the record that the prosecutrix though has stated in her statement under Section 164 Cr.P.C that prosecutrix and present appellant were in relationship but has unequivocally stated in her statement that there was assurance by the present appellant to enter into wedlock.

It is further evident from the statement which is recorded on 29.1.2024 that despite there being an application for registration of marriage which according to appellant was dated 21.12.2023, the appellant has not entered into wedlock.
Therefore, considering the statement of the prosecutrix recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C., this Court is not inclined to enlarge the present appellant on ;anticipatory bail.
5. Accordingly, the present appeal stands dismissed.

MANINDER S. BHATTI) JUDGE vivek Abhishek Kushwaha vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 16 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/70169039/
